options: The deliberate process of combining tables or reintroducing controlled redundancy to improve query performance and analytical usability
A careless shortcut that skips data modelling
The process of removing all redundancy from tables
The process of converting tables to 6NF
The process of encrypting reporting data
questions.explanation: Denormalisation deliberately combines tables or reintroduces controlled redundancy to favour speed, simplicity and workload efficiency.

questions.stem: What is the core idea behind denormalisation?
options: Data should never be normalised in the first place
All tables should be split into single-attribute tables
Once data is properly structured, typically to 3NF or BCNF, certain tables may be merged or attributes duplicated to reduce joins
Redundancy should be eliminated at all costs
Every query should use as many joins as possible
questions.explanation: After data is normalised to around 3NF or BCNF, denormalisation merges tables or duplicates attributes to reduce joins during querying.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a typical denormalisation technique?
options: Pre-calculating derived values
Removing foreign keys entirely
Splitting a table into many smaller tables
Adding a new column each month
Deleting descriptive attributes
questions.explanation: Denormalisation often involves merging related tables into a wider table, duplicating frequently accessed attributes, or pre-calculating derived values.

questions.stem: In which environments are the benefits of denormalisation especially visible?
options: OLTP systems with frequent updates
Source systems with heavy write loads
Message queues
BI and OLAP environments
Version control systems
questions.explanation: In BI and OLAP environments queries run faster with fewer joins and structures are easier for reporting tools and business users to understand.

questions.stem: Which modelling techniques have denormalisation as their structural foundation?
options: Data Vault and Anchor Modelling
NIAM, ORM and FCO-IM
Star schemas, snowflake schemas and Unified Star Schema designs
BPMN and DDD
Taxonomies and ontologies
questions.explanation: Denormalisation forms the structural foundation for Dimensional Modelling techniques such as star, snowflake and Unified Star Schema designs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a trade-off of denormalisation?
options: Redundancy is reintroduced
Updates must be carefully managed to avoid inconsistencies
Storage requirements increase
Queries require more joins
Maintenance challenges in transactional systems
questions.explanation: Denormalisation reduces joins; its trade-offs are redundancy, careful update management, more storage and integrity risks in transactional systems.

questions.stem: In the loan example, what fields might a denormalised LoanFact table contain?
options: Only LoanID and CustID
Only the primary keys of each source table
Server name and partition key
Only the ApprovalStatus
CustomerName, LoanAmount, ProductType, ApprovalStatus, RepaymentDueDate and RepaymentStatus
questions.explanation: A denormalised LoanFact table combines Customer, Loan, ApprovalDecision and RepaymentSchedule information into one structure.

questions.stem: What redundancy appears in the denormalised LoanFact example?
options: LoanID appears once per customer
Each repayment is stored in its own table
ApprovalStatus is stored in a separate lookup
There is no redundancy
CustomerName may appear repeatedly across many rows
questions.explanation: CustomerName may now appear repeatedly across many rows, introducing redundancy that must be managed carefully.

questions.stem: How does denormalisation relate to normalisation?
options: It replaces normalisation
It builds upon normalisation, assuming the logical structure has already been validated
It must be done before normalisation
It is unrelated to normalisation
It reverses 1NF only
questions.explanation: Denormalisation does not replace normalisation; it builds on it, assuming the logical structure and business rules are already validated.

questions.stem: In the modelling journey, what roles do normalisation and denormalisation respectively play at the hinge point?
options: Normalisation enhances performance; denormalisation protects integrity
Normalisation protects integrity; denormalisation enhances usability and performance
Both protect integrity equally
Both are concerned only with storage cost
Normalisation is for OLAP; denormalisation is for OLTP
questions.explanation: Normalisation protects integrity while denormalisation enhances usability and performance; specialised techniques extend one or embrace the other.
